# Pair 003 — Provenance

This is a synthetically authored document pair created for evaluation purposes; it is not a real engineering document. Field naming conventions and units were referenced from publicly uploaded 26-KA-901/26-KA-902 P&ID excerpts for realism only.

## Description

**Equipment:** 26-PA-101 Cooling Water Pump (fictional)  
**Format:** base.pdf is a native text-searchable PDF. **revised.pdf is a SCANNED PDF** (image-only, no text layer) generated by rendering text to an image and embedding it. This exercises the OCR ingestion path (pytesseract).

## Intentional Changes (Rev 0 → Rev 1)

| # | Type | Old Value | New Value |
|---|------|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | Modified | `26-PA-101` | `26-PA-101B` |
| 2 | Modified | `Rated Flow: 250 m3/h` | `Rated Flow: 280 m3/h` |
| 3 | Modified | `Return Temperature: 45 deg C` | `Return Temperature: 42 deg C` |
| 4 | Added | — | `NOTE 3: CHECK VALVE CV-501 INSTALLED DOWNSTREAM` |
| 5 | Removed | `NOTE 2: SUCTION STRAINER BASKET TYPE` | — |

## Expected OCR Behavior

Because revised.pdf goes through OCR:
- Text may be fragmented differently than the original (e.g., title split across multiple lines)
- Confidence scores will be < 1.0 for OCR elements
- Many false positives (spurious adds/removes) are expected due to OCR line fragmentation
- The intentional changes (#1, #2, #3 above) are still detectable because the core numeric/tag content is preserved by OCR
- Change #4 (added note about CV-501) may appear as fragmented adds rather than a single clean add
- This is a realistic representation of scanned document comparison challenges

## Ground Truth Notes

The evaluation ground truth for this pair only includes changes that are reliably detected despite OCR noise. Change #4 (added CHECK VALVE note) is intentionally EXCLUDED from delta_cases.json ground truth because OCR fragments it into multiple unrecognizable pieces — including it would produce a false "missed" that isn't a real engine bug but an OCR limitation. This is documented honestly rather than inflating recall.
